test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following states come under the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fifth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** pertains to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in specific states of India.
 
• The states that come under the **Fifth Schedule** include **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Rajasthan**.
 
• **Jharkhand** and **Chhattisgarh** are among the states with designated Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule. These regions have a significant tribal population, and special provisions are made to protect their rights and socio-economic interests.
 
• The **Fifth Schedule** provides for the establishment of a **Tribes Advisory Council (TAC)** in each of these states to advise on issues relating to the welfare and advancement of Scheduled Tribes.
 
• The purpose of the Fifth Schedule is to ensure self-governance and safeguard the cultural and economic interests of the Scheduled Tribes in these areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fifth Schedule:**

 
 
• The Fifth Schedule is provided in **Article 244(1)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in specific states other than the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, which are covered under the **Sixth Schedule**.
 
• The **President** has the power to declare an area as a Scheduled Area or remove an area from the Scheduled Areas list.
 
• These areas are identified for special governance due to their large tribal population and their unique socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes:**
 
 
• Scheduled Tribes (STs) are communities that are explicitly recognized in the Constitution of India under **Article 342**.
 
• These tribes are provided with special rights and privileges to help them overcome socio-economic and educational disadvantages.
 
• The government implements various welfare schemes and development programs for the upliftment of Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Tribes Advisory Council (TAC):**
 
 
• As per the Fifth Schedule, each state having Scheduled Areas must establish a **Tribes Advisory Council (TAC)**.
 
• The TAC advises the Governor on matters related to the welfare and advancement of Scheduled Tribes in the state.
 
• The Governor has the authority to frame rules for the better governance of Scheduled Areas, following the advice of the TAC.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Fifth and Sixth Schedules:**
 
 
• The Fifth Schedule applies to ten states, including **Jharkhand** and **Chhattisgarh**, while the Sixth Schedule applies to states in the northeastern region such as **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• The Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) with legislative, executive, and judicial powers, while the Fifth Schedule emphasizes the role of the Governor and TAC.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jharkhand:**

 
 
• Jharkhand was formed in **2000** by bifurcating it from Bihar.
 
• The state has a significant population of Scheduled Tribes like **Santhal, Oraon, Munda, Ho**, etc.
 
• It has several **Scheduled Areas** as per the Fifth Schedule to ensure the welfare of tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh:**
 
 
• Chhattisgarh was also formed in **2000** by carving it out of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is home to tribes like **Gond, Baiga, Halba**, and others.
 
• The state has a large number of Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule for safeguarding tribal interests.
 
 
 
• **Other States under Fifth Schedule:**
 
 
• States like **Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan** also have Scheduled Areas.
 
• These areas are designated based on the **high tribal population**, economic backwardness, and lack of adequate infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Safeguards:**
 
 
• The Constitution empowers the **Parliament** to make laws for the protection of tribal interests in Scheduled Areas.
 
• **Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996** (PESA) is an important legislation for the self-governance of tribal communities in Scheduled Areas.
